title: Staging in a cloud, smoke-tested (runbook and check built)
request: Plan staging for the chosen cloud with a cost estimate; after the owner's yes, apply it; then run the end-to-end flows and the browser tests against the staging address and a backup and restore drill. The owner had not yet given a yes, a region, an account or a domain, so build the runbook and the check without touching any account.
spec: tofu plan for staging with a cost estimate; apply only after the owner's yes; product-e2e and the browser tests against staging; a backup and restore drill; production is a separate yes.
plan: Write deploy/STAGING.md in order: decide, tofu plan with the cost, apply only after the owner's yes, the flows, the backup and restore drill, destroy.
Add make staging-check URL=... running the end-to-end flows and the browser checks against an address.
Review with the other kits; the reviewer found the check could not work against a signed-in staging; add bearer-token support to both scripts and correct the claims; commit.
Plan and apply nothing: that needs the provider's credentials and the owner's yes.

decisions.decision: Nothing is planned or applied from the session.
decisions.why: The owner's explicit yes is required before any change to a cloud account, and no account or region was given.

decisions.decision: The runbook says plainly what the check has never been run against.
decisions.why: A smoke test that has only run on an unsigned local server must not be described as proven on staging.

change: New deploy/STAGING.md, a staging-check target in the Makefile, DCLAB_E2E_TOKEN support in scripts/product_e2e.py and scripts/browser_e2e.py, tests/test_staging_check.py.

findings.defect: The staging check could not run against a real staging, and its claims were untrue.
findings.scenario: Staging requires sign-in (the server refuses no sign-in on a host name), and only /api/config and the auth routes are public; the flow scripts sent only the CSRF header, so every flow after /config would get 401. STAGING.md also said 'no model request', but its own step puts the model key into staging, so the flows would send model requests and spend money.
findings.cause: The scripts were written for the local unsigned server; the runbook described the intent, not the behaviour.
findings.fix: Both scripts take an API token of a test member in DCLAB_E2E_TOKEN and send it as a bearer header only when given; STAGING.md, the Makefile and the playbook row say that a configured key means model requests and that the check has never run against a signed-in server.
findings.impact: The owner, following the runbook on a real staging, would have seen every flow after the first fail with 401 and, believing the check sent no model request, would have spent money on model calls with the staging key in place.
findings.open: The check has never run against a signed-in server, so its first real run may still need a fix.

outcome: Runbook and check built (c291a1b), open on the owner's yes, region, account and domain. Nothing planned or applied; the first run against a signed-in server may need a fix.
lessons: A smoke test written against a local server breaks on the first real difference of the target (sign-in); read the target's guard before claiming the check will run there.
A runbook must state the costs its steps cause, such as model requests when a key is configured.
risks: A smoke check written against the local unsigned server will fail against a staging that requires sign-in.
A staging with a model key configured makes real model requests during the flows; the runbook must say so.
Nothing may be planned or applied without the owner's yes, region, account and domain, so the check cannot be proven in this package.
A runbook can describe intent rather than behaviour; every claim in it must match what the scripts do.
